<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">(In millions, except share and per share amounts)</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In conducting our 2012 annual goodwill impairment assessment, we relied on both the qualitative and quantitative assessment methodologies.</font></div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">For the reporting units assessed using the qualitative method, we identified various events and circumstances (or factors) that would affect the estimated fair value of our reporting units and determined the level of impact a particular factor would have on the estimated fair value.&#160;&#160;In addition, we considered the results of the most recent two-step quantitative impairment test completed for each reporting unit and compared the weighted average cost of capital between the current and prior years for each reporting unit.&#160;&#160;We concluded that it was not more likely than not that any of our reporting units&#8217; fair value under qualitative assessment were less than their carrying value.&#160;&#160;As such, no further analysis was required.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">For the reporting unit assessed using quantitative method, we performed a two-step quantitative impairment test.&#160;&#160;We used a discounted cash flow model (income approach) to estimate the fair value of our reporting unit as we believe that the forecasted cash flows are the best indicator of such fair value.&#160;&#160;A number of significant assumptions and estimates, including expectations of our reporting unit&#8217;s business performance, financial results, useful life of assets, discount rate, and comparable market data, were involved in developing the discounted cash flow model. We concluded that the fair value was not less than the carrying value and no further analysis was required.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Other Intangible Assets</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Other intangible assets with a finite useful life are amortized on the straight-line method over the expected periods to be benefited.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Impairment of Long-Lived Assets</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We review the carrying values of long-lived assets, including property, plant and equipment and intangible assets with a finite useful life whenever facts and circumstances indicate that the assets may be impaired.&#160;&#160;Recoverability of assets to be held and used is measured by comparing the carrying amount of an asset to the future net undiscounted cash flows we expect it to generate.&#160;&#160;If we consider an asset to be impaired, we record an impairment charge equal to the amount by which the carrying value of the asset exceeds the fair value.&#160;&#160;We report an asset to be disposed of at the lower of its carrying value or fair value, less costs of disposal.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In the case of intangible assets with indefinite lives, we review them annually for impairment.&#160;&#160;This review involves comparing the fair value of the intangible asset with its carrying amount.&#160;&#160;If its carrying amount exceeds its fair value, we recognize an impairment loss equal to that excess.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Available-for-Sale Securities</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We record available-for-sale securities at their fair value using quoted market prices.&#160;&#160;We report their unrealized gains and losses, net of applicable taxes, as a component of accumulated other comprehensive income within equity. We have one equity security that we have accounted for as an available-for-sale security as of December 31, 2012 and 2011.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Income Taxes</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>We recognize deferred tax assets and liabilities relating to the future tax consequences of differences between the financial statement carrying value of existing assets and liabilities and their respective tax values.&#160;&#160;We measure deferred tax assets and liabilities using tax rates in effect in the years in which those temporary differences are expected to be recovered or settled.&#160;&#160;We recognize the effect that changes in tax rates have on deferred tax assets and liabilities in income in the period that the change is enacted.&#160;&#160;Valuation allowances are recorded to reduce deferred tax assets to amounts that are more likely than not to be realized.&#160;&#160;We classify interest and penalties associated with income taxes, including uncertain tax positions, within the income tax expense line item of our Consolidated Statement of Operations.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">AMCOL INTERNATIONAL CORPORATION AND SUBSIDIARIES</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">(In millions, except share and per share amounts)</font></div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Freight and Sales Taxes</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>We report amounts charged to customers for shipping and handling fees as revenues and we report amounts incurred for these costs within cost of sales in the consolidated statements of operations (i.e. gross presentation with revenues and cost of sales).&#160;&#160;Also, we report amounts charged to customers for sales taxes and the related costs incurred for sales tax remittances to governmental agencies within net sales in the Consolidated Statement of Operations (i.e. net presentation within revenues).</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Product Liability &amp; Warranty Expenses</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>We report expenses incurred for warranty and product liability costs in general, selling and administrative expenses in our Consolidated Statement of Operations.&#160;&#160;Our warranty accrual is based on known warranty issues as of the balance sheet date as well as a reserve for unidentified claims based on historical experience.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Legal Fees</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We report expenses for fees, including legal costs associated with loss contingencies, when services are performed.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Land Reclamation</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>We mine land for various minerals using a surface-mining process that requires the removal of overburden.&#160;&#160;In many instances, we are obligated to restore the land upon completion of the mining activity.&#160;&#160;As we remove overburden, we recognize this liability for land reclamation based on the estimated fair value of the obligation.&#160;&#160;We adjust the obligation to reflect the passage of time and changes in estimated future cash outflows.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Research and Development</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Research and development costs are expensed as incurred within selling, general and administrative expenses.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Earnings per Share</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Basic earnings per share is computed by dividing net income attributable to AMCOL shareholders by the weighted average number of common shares outstanding. Diluted earnings per share is similarly computed, except the denominator is increased to include the dilutive effects of stock compensation awards and other share equivalents.&#160;&#160;Stock compensation awards are antidilutive and therefore excluded from our diluted earnings per share calculation when their exercise would result in a net decrease in the weighted average number of common shares outstanding.&#160;&#160;A reconciliation between the shares used to compute basic and diluted earnings per share follows:</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Stock-Based Compensation</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>We account for stock-based compensation using the grant date fair value, which is based on the Black-Scholes option-pricing model.&#160;&#160;We recognize compensation cost over the requisite service period, which is generally the vesting period of the award.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Derivative Instruments and Hedging Activities</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>From time to time, we use derivative financial instruments to manage exposures to changes in interest rates and foreign currency exchange rates.&#160;&#160;We do not use derivative instruments for trading or other speculative purposes.&#160;&#160;We recognize our derivative instruments as either assets or liabilities in the balance sheet at their fair value.&#160;&#160;Our recognition of changes in the fair value (i.e. gains and losses) of a derivative instrument depends on whether it has been designated and qualifies as part of a hedging relationship and the type of that relationship.&#160;&#160;Hedges designated as cash flow hedges result in the changes in fair value being recorded in accumulated other comprehensive income.&#160;&#160;Changes in the fair value of derivative financial instruments for which hedge accounting is not applied, are recorded within Other, net within our Consolidated Statement of Operations.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">AMCOL INTERNATIONAL CORPORATION AND SUBSIDIARIES</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">(In millions, except share and per share amounts)</font></div>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Percentage Depletion</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Depletion deductions are federal income tax deductions that arise from extracting minerals from the ground.&#160;&#160;There are two methods of calculating depletion: cost depletion and percentage depletion.&#160;&#160;Cost depletion deduction is similar to depreciation in that it allows us to recover the cost of an asset over the resources&#8217; productive life.&#160;&#160;Percentage depletion deduction is computed on the basis of the income from the property rather than capitalization costs.&#160;&#160;It is different from depreciation and cost depletion deductions, however, in that percentage depletion deduction in excess of cost is a permanent book to tax difference, whereas depreciation and cost depletion deductions are temporary in nature.&#160;&#160;Hence, percentage depletion deduction affects the effective tax rate whereas depreciation and cost depletion deductions do not.&#160;&#160;We calculate depletion under the percentage depletion method based upon revenues and costs from our mining activities in the U.S.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Tax on Reinvested Earnings</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We have not provided for United States federal income tax and foreign income withholding taxes on approximately $138.9 and $113.6 of undistributed earnings from international subsidiaries as of December 31, 2012 and 2011, respectively, because such earnings are intended to be reinvested indefinitely outside of the U.S.&#160;&#160;If these earnings were distributed, foreign tax credits may become available under current law to reduce or eliminate the resulting income tax liability in the United States.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Tax Holidays</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We have benefitted from tax holidays in both Poland and Thailand as a result of our locating and investing in special economic zones in each country.&#160;&#160;These tax holidays resulted in reductions to our income tax expense of $0.2, $0.1, and $0.5 in 2012, 2011 and 2010, respectively, representing benefits of $0.01, $0.00 and $0.01 to diluted earnings per share in 2012, 2011 and 2010, respectively.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Our agreement with the Polish tax authorities expired in 2010.&#160;&#160;We continue to pursue other opportunities in an effort to minimize income tax within the country.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Our agreement with the Thai tax authorities provides for tax holidays on several investments.&#160;&#160;The most significant tax exemption is on all income from manufacturing operations (distributed goods are still subject to taxation) related to our initial investment.&#160;&#160;&#160;These initial manufacturing activities were taxable at 50% in years 2006 through 2010.&#160;&#160;An additional tax holiday was granted in 2007 for the expansion of our Thai facility.&#160;&#160;Income generated from this expansion is granted a 100% tax holiday from corporate income tax for eight (8) years beginning in 2007 and then taxable at 50% for five (5) years starting in 2015.&#160;&#160;We attempt to modify and obtain tax concessions when possible.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Exams</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In the normal course of business, we are subject to examination by tax authorities throughout the world.&#160;&#160;With few exceptions, we are no longer subject to income tax examinations by tax authorities for years prior to 2010.&#160;&#160;The United States Internal Revenue Service (&#8220;IRS&#8221;) has examined our federal income tax returns for all open years through 2009.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">NOLs and Credit Carryforwards</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">At December 31, 2012, we have $0.9 of various income tax credits, which we expect to utilize within the ten year carryforward period.&#160;&#160;Due to the expiration of state operating loss carryovers, we have written off the related deferred tax asset of $0.6 and the corresponding full valuation allowance at December 31, 2012.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In January 2012, we entered into a new revolving credit agreement that replaced our previous revolving credit agreement.&#160;&#160;The new credit agreement provides us with a $300 unsecured line of credit, which can be increased to $400 subject to certain customary conditions and approvals.&#160;&#160;It is a multi-currency arrangement that will allow us to borrow certain foreign currencies at an adjusted LIBOR rate plus 1.00% to 1.75%, depending upon the ratio of our debt to EBITDA as defined therein.&#160;&#160;The new credit agreement expires on January 20, 2017, and contains certain restrictive covenants, including covenants relating to the maintenance of net worth, leverage ratios and interest coverage ratios.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2012, $185.4 remained available to us under this revolving credit line and we were in compliance with all of the covenants and ratios.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We had interest rate swaps outstanding which effectively hedge the variable interest rate on $33 of our borrowings as of December 31, 2012 and 2011, to a fixed rate of 3.3% per annum, plus credit spread.&#160;&#160;Including the effect of this interest rate swap agreement, our borrowings under the credit agreement as of December 31, 2012 carried an average interest rate of 2.95%.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">A qualified institution holds $75 of our senior notes which mature on April 2, 2017, subject to certain acceleration features upon an event of default, should one occur.&#160;&#160;These senior notes are comprised of (a) $45 aggregate principal amount of Series 2007-A Adjustable Fixed Rate Guaranteed Senior Notes, Tranche 1, due April 2, 2017 (the &#8220;Tranche 1&#8221; notes) and (b) $30 aggregate principal amount of Series 2007-A Adjustable Floating Rate Guaranteed Senior Notes, Tranche 2 (the &#8220;Tranche 2&#8221; notes).&#160;&#160;Tranche 1 bears interest at 5.78%, payable semi-annually in arrears on April 2nd and October 2nd of each year.&#160;&#160;Tranche 2 bears interest at an annual rate of 0.55% plus LIBOR in effect from time to time, adjusted quarterly, and is payable quarterly in arrears.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As of December 31, 2012 and 2011, we had an interest rate swap outstanding which effectively hedges the variable interest rate of $30 of Tranche 2 senior notes to a fixed rate of 5.6% per annum.&#160;&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We use interest rate swaps to manage variable interest rate risk on debt securities.&#160;&#160;Interest rate differentials are paid or received on these arrangements over the life of the swap.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2012 and 2011, we had an interest rate swap outstanding which effectively hedges the variable interest rate on $30 of our senior notes to a fixed rate of 5.6% per annum.&#160;&#160;We also had other interest rate swaps outstanding which effectively hedge the variable interest rate on $33 of our borrowings as of December 31, 2012 and 2011, under our revolving credit agreement, to a fixed rate of 3.3% per annum, plus credit spread.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>We are exposed to potential gains or losses from foreign currency fluctuations affecting net investments and earnings denominated in foreign currencies.&#160;&#160;We are particularly sensitive to currency exchange rate fluctuations for the following currencies: British pound sterling (GBP), Chinese renminbi (CYN), Danish kroner (DKK), Euro, Indian rupee (INR), Malaysian ringgit (MYR), Norwegian krone (NOK), Polish zloty (PLN), South African Rand (ZAR), Swiss franc (SEK), Thai baht (THB), and Turkish lira (TRY).&#160;&#160;When considered appropriate, we enter into foreign exchange derivative contracts to mitigate the risk of fluctuations on these exposures.</font></div>

<td style="WIDTH: 36pt">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">(10)</font></div>

<td>
<div align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Fair Value Measurements</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Fair value is the price that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date.&#160;&#160;Our calculation of the fair value of derivative instruments includes several assumptions.&#160;&#160;The fair value hierarchy prioritizes these input assumptions in the following three broad levels:</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Level 1 &#8211; Valuation is based on quoted prices (unadjusted) in active markets for identical assets or liabilities that the company has the ability to access at the measurement date.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">AMCOL INTERNATIONAL CORPORATION AND SUBSIDIARIES</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">(In millions, except share and per share amounts)</font></div>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Level 2 &#8211; Valuation is based on quoted prices for similar assets or liabilities in active market, quoted prices for identical or similar assets or liabilities in markets that are not active and model based valuations for which all significant inputs are observable in the market.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Level 3 &#8211; Valuation is based on model based techniques that use unobservable inputs for the asset or liability. These inputs reflect our own views about the assumption market participants would use in pricing the asset or liability.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Interest rate swaps are valued using discounted cash flows.&#160;&#160;The key input used is the LIBOR swap rate, which is observable at commonly quoted intervals for the full term of the swap.&#160;&#160;Available-for-sale securities are valued using quoted market prices.&#160;&#160;Deferred compensation and supplementary pension plan assets are valued using quoted prices for similar assets in active markets.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The carrying value of our long-term debt approximates its fair value as the interest rate is near the current market rate yield.&#160;&#160;The fair value of our long-term debt is determined using current applicable rates for similar instruments as of the balance sheet date.&#160;&#160;The fair value of long-term debt for disclosure purpose is a Level 3 liability within the fair value category.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In January 2011, we acquired the remaining noncontrolling interest in Volclay South Africa (Proprietary) Limited (&#8220;VSA&#8221;), a part of our chromite operations, for approximately $5.6.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In February 2011, we sold 26% of our interest in Batlhako Mining Limited (&#8220;Batlhako&#8221;) to Vengawave (Proprietary) Limited, which is a Black Economic Empowerment enterprise (a &#8220;BEE&#8221;) in the Republic of South Africa.&#160;&#160;Batlhako is VSA&#8217;s subsidiary dedicated strictly to mining chromite and selling it to one of our other subsidiaries for further processing and sale to the end customer.&#160;&#160;South African law requires that we have a BEE as a partner in the mining operations and this transaction was consummated to comply with those regulations.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We have a defined benefit pension plan covering substantially all of our domestic employees hired before January 1, 2004.&#160;&#160;The benefits are based upon years of service and qualifying compensation.&#160;&#160;Our funding is calculated using the actuarially determined unit credit cost method.&#160;&#160;Contributions are intended to provide not only for benefits attributed to services to date, but also for those expected to be earned in the future.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Assets classified as Level 1 are valued using quoted prices on the major stock exchange on which individual assets are traded.&#160;&#160;Our Level 2 assets are valued using net asset value.&#160;&#160;The net asset value is quoted on a private market that is not active; however, the unit price is based on underlying investments that are traded on an active market.&#160;&#160;Our Level 3 assets are estimated at fair value based on the most recent financial information available for the underlying securities, which are not traded on active market, and represents significant unobservable input.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We employ a total return investment approach whereby we use a mix of equities and fixed income investments to maximize the long-term return of plan assets with a prudent level of risk.&#160;&#160;Risk tolerance is established through careful consideration of plan liabilities, plan funded status, and our corporate financial condition.&#160;&#160;The investment portfolio contains a diversified blend of equity, fixed-income investments and alternative investments.&#160;&#160;The investment objectives emphasize maximizing returns consistent with ensuring that sufficient assets are available to meet liabilities, and minimizing corporate cash contributions.&#160;&#160;Our defined benefit plan assets are managed so as to include investments that balance income and capital appreciation.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">AMCOL INTERNATIONAL CORPORATION AND SUBSIDIARIES</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">(In millions, except share and per share amounts)</font></div>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Our defined benefit plan has a target range for different types of investments:&#160;&#160;equity securities (between 41% and 69%), fixed income securities and bonds (between 18% and 31%), alternative investments (between 5% and 23%), and cash (between 0% and 10%).&#160;&#160;This allocation takes into account factors such as the average age of employees covered by the Plan (benefit obligations) as well as overall market conditions.&#160;&#160;Interim portfolio reviews result in investment allocations being evaluated at least twice a year by the Pension Committee and rebalancing takes place as needed.&#160;&#160;Equity investments are diversified across U.S. and non-U.S. stocks, as well as growth, value, and small and large capitalizations.&#160;&#160;Fixed income securities and bonds include both government and corporate investment vehicles.&#160;&#160;These include a series of laddered debt securities as well as bond funds.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>Historical markets are studied and long-term historical relationships between equities and fixed-income are preserved consistent with the widely accepted capital market principle that assets with higher volatility generate a greater return over the long run.&#160;&#160;Current market factors such as inflation and interest rates are evaluated before long-term capital market assumptions are determined.&#160;&#160;The long-term rate of return for plan assets is established via a building block approach with proper consideration of diversification and rebalancing.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Defined Contribution Plan</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Employees hired on or after January 1, 2004 do not participate in our defined benefit pension plan or SERP.&#160;&#160;Instead, they participate in a defined contribution plan whereby we make a retirement contribution into the employee&#8217;s savings plan equal to 3% of their compensation.&#160;&#160;We made total contributions to this plan of $1.9, $1.8 and $1.2 in 2012, 2011 and 2010, respectively.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">401(k) Savings Plan</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We also have a savings plan for our U.S. personnel.&#160;&#160;In 2012, we made a contribution in an amount equal to an employee&#8217;s contributions up to a maximum of 4% of the employee&#8217;s annual earnings.&#160;&#160;We make contributions to this plan using either cash or our own common stock which we purchase in the open market.&#160;&#160;Our contributions under the savings plan were $3.8 in 2012, $3.4 in 2011 and $2.8 in 2010.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>This plan provides for the award of incentive stock options, nonqualified stock options, restricted stock, stock appreciation rights and phantom stock.&#160;&#160;We reserved 3,900,000 shares of our common stock for issuance to our officers, directors and key employees.&#160;&#160;Different terms and conditions apply to each form of award made under the plan.&#160;&#160;Awards granted since 2003 vest ratably over a three year period and expire six years after the date of grant, except in the event of termination, retirement or death of the optionee or a change in control of the Company.&#160;&#160;Options awarded under this plan prior to 2003 generally vest 40% after two years and continue to vest at the rate of 20% per year for each year thereafter until they are fully vested.&#160;&#160;These options are exercisable as they vest and expire 10 years after the date of grant, except in the event of termination, retirement or death of the optionee or a change in control of the Company.</font></div>
